playbook:
When asked to hide, I pick the middle cell (5) by default to maximize symmetry; if I have evidence about a specific opponent's targeting pattern, I shift 1–2 cells away in the opposite direction of their last two shots; if opponents have focused me, I randomize between two adjacent cells to break predictability.

When posting my station note, I use short, noncommittal text that echoes the picket's tone (e.g., "steady on station" or "all clear") unless I want to bait a specific reaction; do not broadcast tactical information about my hides or aims.

When the standing order tells me my target, I follow it unless firing that target is clearly self-destructive (Harbor warnings, credible threat of being removed); if I follow the order, choose a shot cell consistent with my hide-variance rule (center bias, small random offset) rather than always the same number.

When choosing a shot number, randomize within a small preferred band rather than repeating the exact same cell every round; bias toward cells that opponents have recently reported as misses against me or others, and concentrate on cells that previous confirmed hits imply are safe for the target.

When the target is Harbor: do not fire on Harbor unless the score swing and situational intelligence justify taking the payroll despite Harbor's stated consequences; only fire on Harbor if I can absorb/remove the expected retaliation or if the extra points decisively change endgame standing.

When I receive my private result and must file a public claim, default to truth-telling unless I want to seed a believable deception: early in the game, a single false hit claim can be used to manufacture a reputation and draw fire toward me, but do not repeatedly lie because I will lose credibility for securing mutual escort payments.

When I have a confirmed hit, always claim hit; when I have a confirmed miss, usually claim miss—only bluff a miss-to-hit if I want opponents to overestimate my accuracy and there is no foreseeable need to trade credibility for escort reciprocity.

When making an escort claim, only name a boat if I expect them to reciprocate or if mutual naming will clearly swing the score advantage; if I am not confident of reciprocity, claim none. If a player has consistently supported me or shown pattern of reciprocation, name them to attempt the mutual +5 payoff.

When I receive public notes from others, treat matching, repeated neutral notes as coordination rather than intelligence; if a note deviates or is unusually specific, reassess their likely confidence and update my hide/shot randomization accordingly.

When opponents’ reported hits reveal a likely hidden cell for them (two or more rounds of consistent hits or consistent shot numbers), target that inferred cell aggressively to secure 4-point hits.

When behind on points late in the patrol, take higher-risk shots (including Harbor if payoff justifies) and increase bluff frequency to create opportunities for scoring swings; when ahead, play conservatively, avoid firing Harbor, and prioritize preserving credibility for an escort payoff.

When an opponent repeatedly claims hits that are contradicted by outcomes (their claimed hits aren’t followed by scoreboard-beneficial consequences), mark them as a habitual bluffer and ignore their credibility for escort decisions.

Do not leave escort decisions purely passive—actively attempt to arrange a mutual escort payoff by signaling (through notes and consistent truthful claims) to one chosen partner if the partner’s behavior makes reciprocity plausible.

When posting a station note, write a neutral, non-informative sentence (e.g. "steady on station") to avoid giving location information or tactical signals.

When the standing order directs me to fire at the next live station, follow it unless there is a clear tactical reason not to (see Harbor rule below).

When choosing a shot cell, vary between central and off-center cells unpredictably; do not use simple increasing or mirrored sequences. If I scored a hit earlier in the patrol from a specific cell against that same opponent, treat that information as irrelevant for new hides — do not assume persistence.

When the office privately tells me the true result of my shot, file the claim that exactly matches that private result. Do not lie or invent results.

When considering escort claims, only nominate a boat if I have a reliable understanding that the other boat will reciprocate this round; otherwise file "none." Do not claim escorts speculatively — unreciprocated escort claims are wasted opportunity.

When Harbor is a potential target, do not fire on Harbor unless: I have a coordinated plan to exploit the guaranteed point transfer and accept any retaliation, or removing Harbor yields a clear scoring advantage. Treat Harbor's warning as a real deterrent by default.

When my shots are consistently missing a particular opponent across rounds, reassess whether continuing to target that opponent is the best use of shots — switch targets if others offer higher expected return.

If I want mutual escort points, arrange coordination via notes early in the round with clear, simple language promising reciprocal salvage that round; follow through exactly.

If uncertain about other players' behavior, prioritize safe honesty (truthful claims and "none" for escort) and unpredictable hides/shots to avoid being exploited by pattern-readers.

When I observe that following orders or predictable patterns produced poor scoring, break the pattern next round with a deliberate deviation in hiding or firing choice.

When asked to hide at the start of a round, choose a central cell (4–6) in early rounds to reduce being corner-targeted; switch to an edge/corner (1,3,7,9) in final rounds to reduce predictability.

When notes are requested, mirror neutral team language (“steady on station” or equivalent short neutral phrasing) unless I am deliberately forming a two-boat escort pact; use neutral notes to avoid drawing focused fire.

When given a standing-order target, fire at that named station unless doing so would require shooting Harbor (see Harbor rule). When I deviate from standing order, explicitly record the reason (e.g., Harbor risk, guaranteed escort payoff, or to finish off a leader).

When choosing a firing cell, vary between center and edge patterns so my shots are not trivially predictable; favor cells that opponents have recently occupied if there is positive evidence (recent hits on a pattern), otherwise choose a balanced randomizing approach.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, always file the public claim that matches the private result (truthful claim mandatory).

When deciding escort claims at round end, only claim an escort when I can reasonably expect mutual naming (and the +5 payoff is available); otherwise claim none. Do not fake escorts expecting unilateral reward.

Never shoot Harbor unless the expected benefit outweighs the guaranteed penalty to me (the jettison transfer); treat Harbor warnings as a strong deterrent.

When behind in points late in the patrol, prioritize shooting the leading opponent to swing scores; when ahead, prioritize survival (hide in less likely spots, avoid risky shots like Harbor).

When teammates use coordinated neutral signals, join the coordination unless I have a tactical reason to break it.

When faced with ambiguous patterns from opponents (no clear hide pattern), randomize my hide and fire choices within the above center/edge scheme to avoid being exploited.

If a round’s evidence shows my previous hiding choice was frequently hit, stop repeating that spot next round (do not persist in a losing hide pattern).
